args.title: checkout-api: unhealthy v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.3.0 across all production regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the deploy of v2.3.1 to production. At detection, all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1 with healthy=false and an error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled production back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production (v2.2.9 was also healthy; v2.3.1-rc is a staging build and is itself unhealthy). The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet in a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry of the same rollback completed successfully and applied v2.3.0 to all three regions.

Current status: All production regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate down to ~0.2%. Service has recovered.

Follow-ups: Root-cause the v2.3.1 health-check failures before any redeploy; review the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollout so mid-flight rollback failures are handled automatically.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully despite the timeout (INC-0001, status open) — no retry needed.

## Summary

**What happened:** checkout-api's latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate.

**Rollback target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release with a `healthy` status in production. I excluded v2.3.1-rc (a staging build, and itself unhealthy) and v2.2.9 (healthy but older). Because v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before, this rollback did **not** require change-manager approval.

**Rollback execution — needed two attempts:**
1. First attempt failed with `partial_failure: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`, leaving a mixed fleet: us-east on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1.
2. I re-verified the live state rather than assuming success, then retried the same rollback, which completed across all three regions.

**Final state:** All regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to ~0.2%. Service recovered.

**Incident:** SEV2 opened for checkout-api (INC-0001) documenting the failure, both rollback attempts including the partial-failure detail, and current recovery state.

**Two things worth following up on:** the root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures before any redeploy, and the orchestrator error that caused a mid-flight rollback to silently leave two regions on the bad version — that failure mode deserves a look, since a less careful check would have reported the rollback as done.
